title: [DirectX12] [CRASH/LAG] CreateDescriptorHeap fails when using more than few GPUParticles3D
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproducible in 4.4.beta2, 4.3.stable


### System information

Windows 10 , GeForce RTX 3080 Ti, DirectX12

### Issue description

We are running into issues with the DirectX12 backend where using the [GPUParticles3D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_gpuparticles3d.html) type of node.

It seems that creating more than a magic number of particle emitters the DirectX12 backend leads to a crash/error, depending on how these are used.
If the heightmap entity is used this almost directly leads to crashes as there are some code paths there which do not survive a failed allocation.

Otherwise it can lead to GPU memory corruption in serve cases.

[CreateDescriptorHeap](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12device-createdescriptorheap) returns [E_OUTOFMEMORY](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/d3d12-graphics-reference-returnvalues). Even if the GPU/CPU still has free memory available. 

```
ERROR: CreateDescriptorHeap failed with error 0x8007000e.
   at: (drivers\d3d12\rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:347)
ERROR: Method/function failed. Returning: UniformSetID()
   at: uniform_set_create (drivers\d3d12\rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:3884)
ERROR: Condition "!driver_uniform_set" is true. Returning: RID()
   at: uniform_set_create (servers\rendering\rendering_device.cpp:3151)
```

If run with **Vulkan** there does not seem to be such a limit and one can spawn an almost endless amount of particle emitters. 

If using lots of particle emitters with an existing game, this bug seem to trigger after a while depending on how many emitters are active at once but it seems like some resource is also cumulated over time. 
Once this "state" triggers there is nothing we can do to fix it but to restart the game.

Increasing [max_resource_descriptors_per_frame](https://docs.godotengine.org/de/4.x/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-rendering-rendering-device-d3d12-max-resource-descriptors-per-frame) or similar does not seem to change the amount of particle emitters allowed.


We are still getting traces from players >1h  into the game even if we limit the amount of concurrent particle emitters to the absolute minimum. No other backend experiences the same issues.


### Steps to reproduce

Run the example project on a Windows machine it will default to DirectX 12. Notice the errors after a while.

Create a specific amount of GPUParticles3D without deleting them. 
In case of our local GPUs this number seems to be fixed to <800 but this could be a Nvidia specific settings.  From bug reports we know that it affects all GPU vendors. 

In more complex settings it seems that this can also somehow either happen over time, or the number can become way smaller if a game is running instead of only particle emitters.




### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[particlebugminimal.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18676903/particlebugminimal.zip)
